html:
The Kalachuris of Tripuri ruled the Chedi country around today's Jabalpur in central India from about the 7th century to the early 13th. On the 1100 map they hold the upper Narmada valley.

Their capital, Tripuri, lay on the Narmada. They were at their strongest in the 11th century. Gangeyadeva raided widely, and his son Lakshmikarna fought the Palas of Bengal, the Chandelas and the Paramaras, and for a time was the leading king of the north. A related branch ruled from Ratnapura in Chhattisgarh. Another Kalachuri family seized Kalyani from the Western Chalukyas around 1160.

In the 12th century their power ebbed, and by the early 13th century the Tripuri line had vanished from the records.
